title: Give the same plan every run, and record it

expected.says: Run's report for the tiny season matches the expected report

blueprint.signature: def make_plan(season: Season, overrides: tuple[Override, ...] = ()) -> Plan
blueprint.contract: As before, with the solver set from SETTINGS, a module constant: 4 workers that interleave instead of racing, random_seed 7, and max_deterministic_time 10.0 in place of a limit in seconds.
blueprint.idea: Determinism is a setting: interleaved workers, a seed and a limit on deterministic time repeat the same search on every run.

lesson.title: 4.6.3 Deterministic Time, Seeds and Reproducible Runs

blueprint.contract: Returns a value as JSON with sorted keys and no spaces, so equal values give equal text.
blueprint.idea: A hash identifies content only when the content is written one way.

blueprint.signature: def fingerprint(raw: dict, overrides: tuple[Override, ...] = ()) -> str
blueprint.contract: Returns the SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical JSON of {'season': raw, 'overrides': each override's fields as a dictionary}.
blueprint.idea: Equal inputs give equal fingerprints, and any change to the season or the overrides changes it.

blueprint.signature: def plan_record(raw: dict, plan: Plan, overrides: tuple[Override, ...] = ()) -> dict
blueprint.contract: Returns the record of a plan: input_sha256, the OR-Tools version (ortools.__version__), the settings, status, risk_carried, cost, the trims sorted by circuit id as `<cid> on <crew> weeks <first>-<last>`, and the explanation as a list.
blueprint.idea: A record names the input, the solver and its settings, so a difference points at its cause.

blueprint.contract: Returns the record as the text stored and compared: keys sorted, an indent of one, and a newline at the end.
blueprint.idea: Two runs gave the same plan exactly when their records are equal byte for byte.

blueprint.signature: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None
blueprint.contract: With --record, prints the plan's record as dumps writes it, adding no newline of its own; without it, the report as before.
blueprint.idea: A golden file is written by the code itself and reviewed by a person.

cases: the record names its input's fingerprint, the OR-Tools version and the seeded settings
